name: figkit
description: Turn one Figma frame into runnable UI for HTML, Unity, Godot or Cocos Creator — five skills sharing one pixel-faithful IR and one declared interaction layer (modals, guards, list binding).

plugins.name: figma2html
plugins.description: Capture a Figma frame into the FigKit IR and assemble a runnable HTML client: pixel-faithful screens plus declared interactions (modals, guards, list binding). Start here — the other backends consume this capture.

plugins.name: figma2dsl
plugins.description: Turn a captured Figma frame into a semantic UI-DSL markdown document — a readable, diffable description of the screen for design/knowledge layers rather than a runtime.

plugins.name: figma2unity
plugins.description: Compile the FigKit IR into Unity UI Toolkit assets: UXML + USS plus a FlowBinder that implements the shared flow semantics. Verified against Unity 6000.4.8f1.

plugins.name: figma2godot
plugins.description: Compile the FigKit IR into Godot scenes: .tscn plus GDScript flow binder. Verified in Godot 4.3 by pixel-comparing the rendered scene against the HTML backend.

plugins.name: figma2cocos
plugins.description: Compile the FigKit IR for Cocos Creator: a TypeScript interpreter that rebuilds the screen and its declared flow. Runtime type-checks against the official @cocos/creator-types declarations.

plugins.name: figkit-motion
plugins.description: The motion catalog the six backends share: 59 effects (when to use one, when not to), 63 parameter tokens with their calibration status, and 6 algorithms (bezier inversion, analytic spring, momentum projection, rubber-banding, velocity sampling, FLIP). Method and parameters, not a runtime library.
